summary:
ARES PATH is an immersive Mars exploration and astronaut route-planning terminal built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by GAGANTRIX. It combines publicly available NASA Mars science imagery into an interactive mission console: an orbital map of Mars rendered in a Mars-specific equirectangular coordinate system (not Web Mercator), curated science targets, a traverse planner with an honest terrain assessment, and a downloadable mission brief.

Users can switch between verified NASA basemaps (MGS MOLA color hillshade, colorized DEM, HiRISE and CTX mosaics) with live tile telemetry showing loaded vs. missing tiles. Unverified datasets (MOLA roughness, THEMIS, TES) are shown as inspectable "UNAVAILABLE" records — never drawn as if they existed. The route planner lets users pick both traverse endpoints directly on the map, computes great-circle distance and duration, and returns a transparent "INSUFFICIENT" assessment because elevation, slope, and roughness data are not yet available as sampled values. A mission brief with a real PDF download is generated from the route.

Nothing in the interface is invented: coordinates come from real map clicks, distances use haversine on the Mars radius (3,396,190 m), and missing data is labelled unavailable instead of faked.
details:
ARES PATH is a browser-based Mars mission-planning terminal. It renders an orbital map of Mars using a custom Mars equirectangular (plate carrée) CRS — world width 256·2^z px, height half that, no Mercator warp, no latitude wrapping — so tile rows and columns map 1:1 to the geographic graticule. The map is clamped to [-90, -180]…[90, 180] so a drag can never leave the planet.

Basemap layers are radio-selected, one at a time: MGS MOLA color hillshade, Mars colorized DEM, HiRISE mosaic, and CTX mosaic. Each layer shows its source endpoint, resolution, coverage, and measurement type (measured / derived / mosaic / unavailable). A live counter reports loaded vs. missing tiles; missing tiles are reported as coverage gaps in the source product, not silently filled. Three datasets that could not be verified (MOLA surface roughness, THEMIS infrared, TES thermal inertia) are inspectable records marked UNAVAILABLE and are never selectable.

The traverse planner lets the user pick both endpoints by clicking the map (or reset to the Jezero Crater / Aeolis Mons presets), previews the great-circle distance and duration live, and on "CALCULATE ROUTE" computes the distance (haversine on the Mars sphere), duration at an assumed 0.2 m/s suited-walk speed, and an assessment. Because elevation, slope, and surface roughness are not available as sampled values in this build, the assessment returns INSUFFICIENT with an explanation rather than a fabricated score. The traverse can be exported as a mission brief with a deterministic mission ID and a real PDF download.

Tools and technologies: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet (custom Mars CRS), Tailwind CSS, Recharts, jsPDF. No backend; all data comes from public NASA/JPL Mars Trek and Esri OnMars tile services.

How it is creative: it refuses to fabricate. Every number shown (coordinates, distances, durations, tile counts) is derived from real data or clearly labelled as an assumption. The map projection, tiling arithmetic, and data provenance are documented in the README and About page.

Factors considered: scientific integrity (no invented numbers), correct Mars projection (not Earth's Web Mercator), honest handling of missing data, responsive layout (panels collapse to toggles at any width; drawers below 1024 px), accessibility of controls (visible +/−/reset zoom buttons), and performance (lazy-loaded PDF library, invalidates map size on resize).
